The usual misreading takes the aphorism to mean that status has been wholly replaced by contract, so that modern law has no fixed or inherited positions left. Maine meant something narrower: the dominant basis of legal rights and duties moved from a person's ascribed place in the family group to voluntary agreements between individuals presumed free and equal. He also treated this as an observed tendency, not an inevitable law, and he recognised that status-like relations, such as family ties, persist within contract societies.
CONFIDENCE: 82
